messages.subject: [GSoC-R] Schedules, Deliverables, Next Steps
parts:
Student applications for GSoC 2017 close on Monday, April 3rd at 16:00
UTC.

Google's deadlines are firm, and there are no exceptions, for any
reason.

Students:
You should be communicating as much as possible with the mentors for
your desired project and revising your applications. Waiting till the
last minute is not usually a sign of a project likely to succeed.
Please try to finalize your application and upload the final PDF well
in advance of the deadline, after addressing any questions or comments
from your mentors or any other R project mentor. Applications are
fixed after the final PDF is uploaded.

Mentors:
Some mentors have not accepted their invitations. If you're having
trouble, please contact Toby or me immediately, and we'll try to help
you.  

Right Now: You should be communicating with your applicants about their
applications. Please raise any and all concerns that you have about
the application using comments in the Google doc, per Google
guidelines. Give your students as much feedback as you can on the
application, while they still have time to make it better.

After April 3rd, Toby and I will be doing a first review of submitted
applications. We will be contacting mentors individually for feedback
where necessary. After April 3rd, we also need you to do a few things
on the Google Summer of Code system:

1> We need you to select 'Want to Mentor' on an application for a
project where you are listed as a mentor, or on the strongest
application for the project where there are multiple applications for a
single project.

2> We also need you to comment on all applications for projects where
you are listed as a mentor in the 'Comment on this Proposal' section at
the bottom of the proposal page. Please provide a succinct summary of
your feelings on the application. These comments are visible to other
R mentors only, not to the students. We want all mentors to comment on
all proposals for a project you are a listed mentor for.

3> We *want*, but cannot require, that you comment on other student
applications for proposed projects that you will not be mentoring this
summer. If you have time to comment on draft applications this weekend
in your area of expertise, please do so to help out the students in
thinking about their projects. In any case, please comment on projects
next week where you have some expertise. Google used to require all
mentors to vote on applications, but that was removed from the process
last year. Your input is still very valuable to Toby and me as we
review applications and make slot requests.

Slot request to Google will happen no later than April 17th, per the
Google Deadline. April 19th-24th Toby and I will communicate with
mentors and allocate the slots we've received from Google.

On May 4th, accepted projects will be announced by Google.

Between April 3rd and May 4th, Google prohibits mentors and
organizations from telling students whether or not their proposal has
been accepted. Students, please don't ask. Mentors, please don't
tell. Google takes a very dim view of breaking this rule.

Regards,

Brian
